json.title: Postgres CDC: error when syncing inherited tables where child has different schema than parent
json.body:
### Summary
When running Postgres CDC with `PEERDB_POSTGRES_CDC_HANDLE_INHERITANCE_FOR_NON_PARTITIONED_TABLES` enabled and the source uses old-style `INHERITS` tables (not declarative partitioning), child tables with **extra columns** beyond the parent's schema cause tuple decoding failures or cross-child data corruption.

Unlike partitioned tables where all partitions share an identical column layout, `INHERITS` children can add their own columns (e.g. `stripe_payment` inherits 18 columns from `payment` and adds `fk_stripe_payment` and `stripe_account_id`). The WAL emits tuples using the child's column layout, but PeerDB was decoding them using the wrong RelationMessage.

### Root cause
When a child table's `RelationMessage` arrived in the WAL stream, `processMessage` mutated `msg.RelationID` from the child's ID to the parent's:
```go
msg.RelationID, err = p.checkIfUnknownTableInherits(ctx, msg.RelationID)
```
This caused `processRelationMessage` to store the child's RelationMessage under the **parent's** relation ID:
```go
p.relationMessageMapping[currRel.RelationID] = currRel  // stored under parent's ID
```
Then in `processInsertMessage` / `processUpdateMessage` / `processDeleteMessage`, the RelationMessage was looked up using the parent's ID:
```go
rel, ok := p.relationMessageMapping[relID]  // relID = parent's ID
```
This had two consequences:
1. **Cross-child contamination**: multiple children's RelationMessages overwrote each other under the same parent key — whichever child sent last determined the column layout used for all children.
2. **Positional mismatch**: a child with extra columns (e.g. 20 columns) had its tuple decoded using a RelationMessage from a different child or the parent (e.g. 18 columns), causing columns to be decoded with the wrong types.

### Fix
- Stop mutating `msg.RelationID` in the `RelationMessage` handler. Store each child's RelationMessage under its **own** relation ID.
- In `processInsertMessage` / `processUpdateMessage` / `processDeleteMessage`, use the child's actual relation ID (`actualRelID`) for RelationMessage lookup (correct tuple decoding), and the parent's relation ID (`relID`) only for table name and destination routing.
- In `processRelationMessage`, resolve to the parent via `getParentRelIDIfPartitioned` for name/schema lookups, but leave `currRel.RelationID` untouched for storage.

Hello @jgao54 and @heavycrystal!

We hit this issue at scale and would like to help get it fixed. Our Postgres is schema-per-tenant: each tenant table `INHERIT`s a shared parent, with about 3,150 children per parent. Because tenants were created at different points in our migration history, their column orders have drifted; our largest table has 39 distinct column orders across its children. With the parent's RelationMessage slot shared by all children, we see both failure modes: mirrors stalling on `tuple has more columns than the last RelationMessage`, and, worse, silent swaps when two children have the same column count in a different order (e.g., `name` and `val` exchanged in ClickHouse).

I have a fix ready that takes the same approach as #4045 and the first commit of #3936: each RelationMessage is stored under the relid its tuples arrive with, and a tuple whose column count does not match its RelationMessage is rejected instead of being decoded misaligned. The change in `cdc.go` is about 50 lines. It comes with unit tests and Tilt e2e tests for divergent child layouts (a swapped order, an extra column, interleaved CDC, a restart, child DDL, a child added after start) and for partitions published both via the root and as leaves. I confirmed that the e2e tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. You can preview it as a draft PR on my fork: [CHeavyarms/peerdb#1](https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/1).

On the two concerns from #3936:

> it's just pushing the error to a different place

This fix is only about column order; PostgreSQL already guarantees that inherited columns keep the parent's types. Child-only columns are still added to the destination as nullable columns, exactly as today.

> if `pg_attribute` doesn't contain the column when querying, the schema change won't be propagated

Nothing is filtered on `pg_attribute`. Every column a RelationMessage carries is propagated as on `main`.

How would you prefer to proceed?

1. I open a small PR with the core fix and tests, crediting #4045 and #3936.
2. I contribute the tests to #4045, if you would rather land that one.

I also have four follow-ups ready. They are stacked as drafts on my fork, each showing only its own commit, so you can preview them now; I will hold them here until the core fix is settled:

1. Hardening for hierarchies with many children: the same parent choice at pull start and at runtime discovery, and one added-column delta per pull instead of one per child ([CHeavyarms/peerdb#2](https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/2)).
2. A flow warning for hierarchies deeper than one level, whose deeper descendants CDC does not replicate ([CHeavyarms/peerdb#4](https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/4)).
3. A small fix that reserves `_peerdb_source_schema` while `PEERDB_SOURCE_SCHEMA_AS_DESTINATION_COLUMN` is on; today a source column with that name is silently overwritten ([CHeavyarms/peerdb#5](https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/5)).
4. A feature for schema-per-tenant fan-in: behind a new internal version, that setting would stamp each inheritance child's own schema instead of the parent's, in CDC and in the snapshot ([CHeavyarms/peerdb#3](https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/3)). Would that be a direction you are open to? I am happy to open a separate issue with the design and benchmarks.

Happy to adjust to whatever is easiest for you to review. Thank you.
Following up on this, https://github.com/CHeavyarms/peerdb/pull/1 looks ready-to-merge (see nit comments). Thank you @CHeavyarms  and @lukejudd-lux for your contributions.
